paper.core_task: analyzing gating mechanisms in softmax attention layers

contributions.name: A systematic analysis of gating positions in softmax attention
contributions.author_claim_text: In this work, we investigate gating mechanisms in the standard softmax attention. Specifically, we introduce gating at distinct positions: after the query, key, and value projections; following the Scaled Dot Product Attention outputs; and after the final dense output layer.
contributions.description: The paper systematically explores applying gating at five different positions within the attention layer, evaluating various forms like elementwise/headwise, head-specific/head-shared, and additive/multiplicative.

contributions.name: Identification of non-linearity and sparsity as key factors
contributions.author_claim_text: We identify two factors contributing to the efficacy of gating: (i) Non-Linearity. The two consecutive linear layers can be rewritten into one low-rank linear projection. Therefore, introducing non-linearity through gating can increase the expressiveness. (ii) Sparsity. contributions.name: An attention-sink-free model via sparse SDPA gating
contributions.author_claim_text: Sparse gating eliminates the massive activation and attention sink. These models demonstrate superior performance in length generalization, achieving a gain of over 10 points on RULER.
contributions.description: Applying sparse gating after the SDPA output eliminates attention sink and massive activation phenomena, leading to improved training stability and better generalization to longer context lengths.

novelty_claims.text: The paper lacks a clear and upfront articulation of its novel contributions, which limits the immediate impact of the work.
The paper makes a valuable contribution by systematically analyzing the impact of different gating mechanisms within attention layers, which is a relatively underexplored area.
